blocks.text: MANILA – The Bureau of Customs (BOC) has scrapped the requirement for prior clearance from its Imports Assessment Service (IAS) when the requirement is based solely on a commodity’s classification or tariff heading. Commissioner Charlito Martin Mendoza issued OCOM Memorandum Order 124-2026 on Wednesday, removing mandatory prior clearance from the IAS when required solely on the basis of commodity classification or tariff heading. “Our goal is to bring down the cost of doing business in the country. For importers, this reform could reduce cargo processing time by three days. That means faster movement of goods and lower logistics costs,” he said […]...
